subject: SIG questionnaire initiation & SOC 2 clarifications - NovaCare
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novacare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: SIG questionnaire initiation & SOC 2 clarifications - NovaCare

Hi Samir / Emily —

Thanks again for the time today — great to learn more about NovaCare's integration plans. As discussed, I'm kicking off the vendor security questionnaire so your security team can review our controls. I've attached the SIG-lite request we typically use (NovaCare_SIG_Request.pdf).

Quick recap / asks:
- Can you confirm which questionnaire you prefer (SIG, CAIQ, or a custom form)? The attached is our SIG-lite.
- SOC 2: we are SOC 2 Type II audited. Can you confirm whether you need the full report (redacted) or a SOC 2 summary is sufficient for initial review?
- Compliance scope: are GDPR/HIPAA controls required for this engagement? You mentioned HIPAA coverage in the call — do you require a BAA?
- Data residency: any specific region constraints (US-only, EU)?
- Subprocessors: if you need the subprocessor list, we can provide the most recent register or a link.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please confirm which questionnaire/form you prefer.
2) If SIG is fine, I'll send the SIG template pre-filled with our responses and a HubSpot/Drive upload link so your team can add answers.
3) If you want the SOC 2 report, let me know and we'll share a redacted report over a secure link.

Can you aim to get us confirmation on the questionnaire type and whether a SOC 2 summary is OK by EOD 8/17? We'll try to turn around any follow-ups within 48 hours.

Attachments: NovaCare_SIG_Request.pdf

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novacare.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Wong <emily.wong@novacare.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T13:04:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire initiation & SOC 2 clarifications - NovaCare

Hi Camila —

Appreciate the recap and the attachment. SIG sounds good to us; we'll use the SIG-lite as a starting point. A couple of clarifying questions from our side before we start filling: 

1) SOC 2: We do require evidence of SOC 2 Type II. For initial risk screening, would a Redwood SOC 2 summary be acceptable or do we need the full redacted report? If the redacted report is required, what is the secure delivery method?

2) HIPAA / BAA: NovaCare handles PHI for some customers. We will require a BAA if you process or store PHI. Does Redwood sign BAAs for hosted API customers?

3) Data residency: our pilot will store data in the US, but we may have EU clients later. Can you provide options for regional isolation (US-only, EU-only)?

4) Subprocessors: please send the current subprocessor list or a link.

We can start populating the SIG this week. If you can pre-fill any sections, that would save time.

Thanks —
Samir Patel
Director, Security & Privacy (NovaCare)
samir.patel@novacare.com

Hi Samir —

Thanks — SIG is perfect. I've attached a pre-filled SIG template (Redwood_SIG_Template_filled.xlsx) to accelerate review and a short SOC 2 summary (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf).

Answers to your clarifying Qs: 
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II (most recent audit period ends 2025-12-31). For initial screening the summary should be fine. If you need the full redacted report, we can share it via secure Docusign/ShareFile link — let me know and I'll initiate.
- BAA / HIPAA: Yes, we sign BAAs for customers that require it. Our standard BAA is provided under the Data & Security section of the PSA; legal can route a countersigned copy.
- Data residency: We support region-specific deployments (US-only or EU-only) for Dedicated/Private customers. For hosted API we can set region routing for data residency controls; we'll share the options and any contractual language needed.
- Subprocessors: attached link to our current subprocessors in the notes below.

Practical next steps:
1) I'll upload the pre-filled SIG to the HubSpot deal record and to a shared Drive link (see related links). Please have your security team add missing details on the template.
2) If you need the redacted SOC 2, reply here and I'll start the secure share process.
3) If PHI is in scope, confirm and we'll escalate to legal for a BAA draft.

Looping Logan (cc) for any technical details around encryption, key management, and data flows.

Attachments: Redwood_SIG_Template_filled.xlsx, Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf

Best —

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-17T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire initiation & SOC 2 clarifications - NovaCare

Hi Samir —

Following up with technical clarifications from our side. Quick answers you can paste into the SIG where relevant: 

- SOC 2: SOC 2 Type II (audit period through 2025-12-31). We can provide a redacted report via secure ShareFile; let Camila know and she'll initiate.
- Encryption at rest: AES-256 by default. Keys are managed in Redwood's cloud KMS; we also support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Dedicated/Private deployments — specify requirement in the SIG and we'll provide config details.
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+ (recommend TLS 1.3 where supported).
- Key management: KMS (Redwood-managed) with HSM-backed KMS for Dedicated/Private; BYOK via KMS integration available.
- Subprocessors: full list at https://redwood.example.com/subprocessors (public list). If you need an export for procurement, I can generate a CSV.
- PHI / BAA: Redwood signs BAAs for customers that require it. For hosted customers that handle PHI, we recommend using Dedicated/Private deployment models; legal will scope the BAA accordingly.
- Data retention & deletion: default retention for request logs and KV cache is 30 days; configurable via contract for Dedicated/Private. We support data deletion requests and provide audit logs on deletion upon request.
- Penetration testing & vulnerability management: annual 3rd-party pentests and a regular patching cadence; details are in the SOC 2 summary.

If you want, I can join a short call with your security team to walk through the SIG answers.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
